definition: A prompting framework that interleaves reasoning steps ('thoughts') with concrete actions (like tool calls), letting a model reason about what to do and then act, in an iterative loop.
details: ReAct (Reason + Act) combines chain-of-thought-style reasoning with tool use, allowing models to gather new information via actions and incorporate it into subsequent reasoning steps, a pattern widely adopted in agentic LLM systems.
story: Imagine handing a to-do list to a very clever intern who refuses to guess: before each step, they look around, check the result, and adjust. It is the difference between a search engine and a helper who actually finishes the task. The machine stops just answering one question and starts getting a job done, step by step, checking its work along the way. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is ReAct.

citation.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
